history.period: 15th century (built c. 1467-1475; sources differ on the exact year)
history.summary: The Vishnu Temple of Bishnupur is the oldest brick Vishnu temple in Manipur and a protected historical monument (ASI/Ministry of H.R.D., Government of India). After King Senbi Kiyamba (born Thangwai Ningthouba) conquered Kyang in the Kabaw Valley in alliance with Chaopha Khe Khomba, king of Pong (Shan kingdom, upper Burma), the Pong king presented him with a sacred stone/image called Pheiya; a Brahmin identified it as Lord Vishnu and said good fortune would follow if rice boiled in cow's milk was offered to it. Kiyamba installed the image at his capital Lamangdong and built a brick temple there - tradition dates this to 1467/1475 - and Lamangdong was renamed Vishnupur/Bishnupur (abode of Vishnu). The temple shows a synthesis of Bengali (Char-Chala hut-type) and Southeast Asian (Burmese/Javanese) features, with Chinese-influenced elements noted by visitors. CONFLICTS: (1) build attribution is contested - commonly attributed to Kiyamba (1467-1508), but one architectural study argues material and literary evidence points to the Charairongba period (1697-1709); (2) Wikipedia's Bishnupur town article says the town's naming is likely from the Bhagyachandra era (18th century), conflicting with the 15th-century Lamangdong-renaming narrative - (verify). CSV town/state/district (Bishnupur, Bishnupur district, Manipur) are correct.

name: Vishnu Temple
town_description: Bishnupur (Lamangdong in ancient times) is the headquarters of Bishnupur district, Manipur, about 27 km south of Imphal on the Tiddim Road (24.6333N, 93.7667E per Wikipedia). It derives its name from this ancient Vishnu temple. The bustling town is known for stoneware production, hill-grown oranges, yongchak (tree beans), vegetables and shoibum (fermented bamboo shoot); nearby attractions include Loktak Lake, Keibul Lamjao National Park and the Loukoipat ecological park.
tradition: Vaishnavism (early Vishnu worship of the Kiyamba era; Vaishnavism became the state religion of Manipur later, under Charairongba in 1704 and Garib Niwaz in the 18th century)

travel.airport: Imphal International Airport, about 27 km away (less than an hour's drive per MakeMyTrip - verify).
travel.railway: No railway station at Bishnupur; the nearest long-standing railhead is Dimapur (~215 km - verify; status of the Jiribam-Imphal line - verify).
travel.road: 27 km south of Imphal on the Tiddim Road; reachable by bus and shared taxi from Imphal (verify current services).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (typical Manipur dry season).
visitor_information.opening_hours: No official timings published (verify). One visitor review notes the temple interior may be closed at times while the structure can be viewed from outside; as an ASI-protected monument it is best visited in daylight hours. Remove shoes before entering, per local custom.
